diagnose.sql: SHOW GLOBAL STATUS WHERE Variable_name IN ('Threads_connected','Max_used_connections')
diagnose.look_for: Threads_connected close to max_connections

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'max_connections'
diagnose.look_for: the limit

diagnose.sql: SELECT USER, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(COMMAND = 'Sleep') AS sleeping FROM information_schema.PROCESSLIST GROUP BY USER ORDER BY n DESC
diagnose.look_for: one app user holding many sleeping connections

diagnose.sql: SELECT usename, state, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC
diagnose.look_for: many 'idle' or 'idle in transaction' connections

diagnose.sql: SHOW max_connections
diagnose.look_for: the limit

causes.title_en: The app opens connections and doesn't close them (many sleeping/idle ones)
causes.title_hi: App connection kholti hai par band nahi karti (bahut saare sleeping/idle)

causes.title_en: Real traffic is higher than the limit
causes.title_hi: Asli traffic limit se zyada hai

causes.title_en: Slow queries keep connections busy, so new requests pile up
causes.title_hi: Slow queries connection pakde rehti hain, nayi requests line mein lag jaati hain

fixes.steps_en: Lower wait_timeout (MySQL) / set idle_session_timeout (PostgreSQL 14+) so idle connections close; fix persistent connections in the app.
fixes.steps_hi: wait_timeout kam karo (MySQL) / idle_session_timeout set karo (PostgreSQL 14+) taaki idle connection band ho; app ke persistent connections theek karo.

fixes.steps_en: Raise max_connections carefully (each connection uses memory), or add a pooler (ProxySQL / PgBouncer).
fixes.steps_hi: max_connections dhyan se badhao (har connection memory leta hai), ya pooler lagao (ProxySQL / PgBouncer).

fixes.steps_en: Open the Live tab, find the slow queries and run them through the query fixer.
fixes.steps_hi: Live tab kholo, slow queries dhoondo aur unhe query fixer se theek karo.

verify.en: Threads_connected / active connections stay well under the limit for a day.
verify.hi: Ek din tak connections limit se kaafi neeche rahein.

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE, IS_GRANTABLE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: accounts you don't know, '%' hosts (any computer), and SUPER / FILE / GRANT OPTION / CREATE USER given to app users

diagnose.sql: SELECT USER, HOST, DB, COMMAND, TIME FROM information_schema.PROCESSLIST ORDER BY TIME DESC
diagnose.look_for: sessions from an IP/host that isn't your app server or your office

diagnose.sql: SELECT TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_TIMING, CREATED, DEFINER, LEFT(ACTION_STATEMENT, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.TRIGGERS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: a trigger nobody on your team made, especially on comments/users/usermeta/posts/orders, or one that writes into a users table

diagnose.sql: SELECT EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME, DEFINER, STATUS, EVENT_TYPE, INTERVAL_VALUE, INTERVAL_FIELD, CREATED, LAST_EXECUTED, LEFT(EVENT_DEFINITION, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.EVENTS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: scheduled events you didn't create (they can re-add a user, re-insert spam or delete data every few minutes)

diagnose.sql: SELECT ROUTINE_SCHEMA, ROUTINE_NAME, ROUTINE_TYPE, DEFINER, SECURITY_TYPE, CREATED, LAST_ALTERED FROM information_schema.ROUTINES WHERE ROUTINE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('sys', 'mysql') ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: procedures/functions with names you don't recognise, recently created, or with an unknown DEFINER

diagnose.sql: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, CREATE_TIME, TABLE_ROWS FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%recover%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%readme%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%read_me%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%warning%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%bitcoin%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%ransom%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%hacked%' OR LOWER(TABLE_SCHEMA) LIKE '%recover%' OR LOWER(TABLE_SCHEMA) LIKE '%readme%' OR LOWER(TABLE_SCHEMA) LIKE '%read_me%'
diagnose.look_for: a table/database like RECOVER_YOUR_DATA, README, PLEASE_READ_ME or WARNING: that is the ransom note

diagnose.sql: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, TABLE_ROWS, CREATE_TIME, UPDATE_TIME FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY CREATE_TIME DESC LIMIT 30
diagnose.look_for: tables created recently that nobody made, or important tables now with 0 rows

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('bind_address', 'skip_networking', 'port', 'require_secure_transport', 'local_infile', 'secure_file_priv')
diagnose.look_for: bind_address 0.0.0.0 or * (open to every network), local_infile ON, secure_file_priv empty

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin, rolreplication, rolbypassrls, rolvaliduntil FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname NOT LIKE 'pg\_%' ORDER BY rolsuper DESC, rolname
diagnose.look_for: a login role you don't know, or extra roles with superuser / createrole / bypassrls

diagnose.sql: SELECT g.rolname AS powerful_role, r.rolname AS member FROM pg_auth_members m JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = m.member JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid WHERE g.rolname IN ('pg_execute_server_program', 'pg_read_server_files', 'pg_write_server_files', 'pg_signal_backend', 'pg_read_all_data', 'pg_write_all_data')
diagnose.look_for: an app or unknown role allowed to run server programs or read/write server files

diagnose.sql: SELECT usename, client_addr, application_name, backend_start, state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'client backend' ORDER BY backend_start
diagnose.look_for: connections from addresses that aren't your app or office, or a strange application_name

diagnose.sql: SELECT evtname, evtevent, evtowner::regrole AS owner, evtfoid::regproc AS runs_function, evtenabled FROM pg_event_trigger
diagnose.look_for: any event trigger you didn't create (they fire on CREATE/DROP/ALTER in the whole database)

diagnose.sql: SELECT t.tgrelid::regclass AS on_table, t.tgname, t.tgfoid::regproc AS runs_function, t.tgenabled FROM pg_trigger t WHERE NOT t.tgisinternal ORDER BY 1
diagnose.look_for: a trigger you don't know, especially one running a function you didn't write

diagnose.sql: SELECT table_schema, table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE lower(table_name) LIKE '%recover%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%readme%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%read_me%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%warning%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%bitcoin%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%ransom%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%hacked%'
diagnose.look_for: a ransom-note table (README, RECOVER_YOUR_DATA, WARNING...) in this database

diagnose.sql: SELECT datname, pg_database_size(datname) AS bytes FROM pg_database WHERE NOT datistemplate ORDER BY datname
diagnose.look_for: a new database like readme_to_recover, or your database suddenly tiny

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('listen_addresses', 'port', 'ssl', 'password_encryption', 'log_connections', 'log_statement')
diagnose.look_for: listen_addresses '*' (open to every network), md5 passwords, connection logging off

causes.title_en: An account or permission exists that nobody on your team created
causes.title_hi: Koi account ya permission hai jo aapki team ne nahi banaya

causes.title_en: Triggers, scheduled events or procedures were planted to keep access or change data
causes.title_hi: Triggers, scheduled events ya procedures daale gaye hain taaki access bana rahe ya data badle

causes.title_en: Data was deleted and a ransom note left
causes.title_hi: Data delete karke ransom note chhoda gaya

causes.title_en: The database is open to the whole internet
causes.title_hi: Database poore internet ke liye khula hai

causes.title_en: Nothing suspicious found: the change came from a plugin, update or teammate
causes.title_hi: Kuch shak wala nahi mila: badlaav plugin, update ya team ke kisi member se aaya

fixes.steps_en: Treat it as a break-in: follow 'Hacked: what to do right now' (copy for evidence, change every password, remove the unknown account).
fixes.steps_hi: Ise break-in maano: 'Hack ho gaya: abhi turant kya karein' follow karo (saboot ke liye copy, har password badlo, anjaan account hatao).

fixes.steps_en: Open the 'unknown triggers' or 'unknown scheduled events/procedures' playbook and remove only what you have confirmed is not yours.
fixes.steps_hi: 'Anjaan triggers' ya 'anjaan scheduled events/procedures' playbook kholo aur sirf wahi hatao jo pakka aapka nahi hai.

fixes.steps_en: Don't pay. Follow the ransom-note playbook: keep the note as evidence, close access, restore from your backup.
fixes.steps_hi: Paise mat do. Ransom-note playbook follow karo: note saboot ke liye rakho, access band karo, backup se restore karo.

fixes.steps_en: Make the database listen only on the private network/localhost and allow its port only from your app server in the firewall.
fixes.steps_hi: Database ko sirf private network/localhost pe sunne do aur firewall mein port sirf app server ke liye kholo.

fixes.steps_en: Keep the check results; turn on connection/query logging so a real break-in would be visible next time.
fixes.steps_hi: Check ke results rakh lo; connection/query logging on karo taaki agli baar asli break-in dikh jaye.

verify.en: Every account, trigger, event and procedure in the results is known to your team, and no ransom table exists.
verify.hi: Results mein har account, trigger, event aur procedure aapki team ka jaana-pehchana hai, aur koi ransom table nahi hai.

causes.title_en: The attacker may still be connected or able to log in
causes.title_hi: Attacker abhi bhi connected ho sakta hai ya login kar sakta hai

causes.title_en: The database and app passwords must be treated as stolen
causes.title_hi: Database aur app ke passwords ko chori hua maano

causes.title_en: The database port is reachable from the internet
causes.title_hi: Database ka port internet se pahuncha ja sakta hai

fixes.steps_en: 1) Take a full copy (dump or disk snapshot) of the database AS IT IS now and keep it aside as evidence; don't clean before this. 2) Note the time you noticed it. 3) Put the site in maintenance mode so customers aren't served infected pages.
fixes.steps_hi: 1) Database ki abhi jaisi hai waisi poori copy (dump ya disk snapshot) lo aur saboot ke liye alag rakho; isse pehle safai mat karo. 2) Kab pata chala, time likh lo. 3) Site maintenance mode mein daalo taaki customers ko infected page na dikhe.

fixes.steps_en: Change the password of every database account (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY / ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD), put the new app password in the app config (wp-config.php, .env), change hosting/cPanel/SSH/FTP and admin-panel passwords, and replace the WordPress secret keys so every session is logged out.
fixes.steps_hi: Har database account ka password badlo (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY / ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD), naya app password config mein daalo (wp-config.php, .env), hosting/cPanel/SSH/FTP aur admin panel ke password badlo, aur WordPress secret keys badlo taaki sab log out ho jayein.

fixes.steps_en: Close the port to the internet now: bind the server to localhost/private IP (bind_address / listen_addresses), allow only your app server in the firewall, and remove accounts that can log in from any host ('%').
fixes.steps_hi: Port abhi internet ke liye band karo: server ko localhost/private IP pe bind karo (bind_address / listen_addresses), firewall mein sirf app server allow karo, aur jo account kisi bhi host ('%') se login kar sakte hain unhe hatao.

verify.en: Only your app and your team's known accounts are connected; old passwords no longer work; the port can't be reached from outside.
verify.hi: Sirf aapki app aur team ke jaane-pehchane account connected hain; purane password kaam nahi karte; bahar se port nahi khulta.

diagnose.sql: SELECT u.ID, u.user_login, u.display_name, u.user_registered FROM wp_users u JOIN wp_usermeta m ON m.user_id = u.ID WHERE m.meta_key LIKE '%capabilities' AND m.meta_value LIKE '%administrator%' ORDER BY u.user_registered DESC
diagnose.look_for: an administrator you don't know, or one 'registered' on an odd date (attackers often fake an old date)

diagnose.sql: SELECT m.user_id, m.meta_key, m.meta_value, u.user_login FROM wp_usermeta m LEFT JOIN wp_users u ON u.ID = m.user_id WHERE (m.meta_key LIKE '%capabilities' AND m.meta_value LIKE '%administrator%') OR (m.meta_key LIKE '%user_level' AND m.meta_value = '10')
diagnose.look_for: admin rights given to a user id that has no row in wp_users (user_login empty) or to a user you don't recognise

diagnose.sql: SELECT ID, user_login, display_name, user_registered FROM wp_users ORDER BY ID DESC LIMIT 20
diagnose.look_for: the newest user ids: a high id with an old registration date was added later and back-dated

diagnose.sql: SELECT option_name, LEFT(option_value, 200) AS value FROM wp_options WHERE option_name IN ('siteurl', 'home', 'admin_email', 'users_can_register', 'default_role', 'template', 'stylesheet')
diagnose.look_for: siteurl/home pointing to a strange domain, admin_email you don't own, users_can_register = 1 together with default_role = administrator

diagnose.sql: SELECT TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_TIMING, CREATED, DEFINER, LEFT(ACTION_STATEMENT, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.TRIGGERS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: a trigger nobody on your team made, especially on comments/users/usermeta/posts/orders, or one that writes into a users table

diagnose.sql: SELECT EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME, DEFINER, STATUS, EVENT_TYPE, INTERVAL_VALUE, INTERVAL_FIELD, CREATED, LAST_EXECUTED, LEFT(EVENT_DEFINITION, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.EVENTS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: scheduled events you didn't create (they can re-add a user, re-insert spam or delete data every few minutes)

causes.title_en: An attacker added an administrator account
causes.title_hi: Attacker ne administrator account jod diya

causes.title_en: Admin rights were written straight into wp_usermeta (sometimes for a user id that isn't in wp_users)
causes.title_hi: Admin rights seedhe wp_usermeta mein likh diye (kabhi aise user id ke liye jo wp_users mein hai hi nahi)

causes.title_en: A trigger, event or infected file re-creates the admin after you delete it
causes.title_hi: Koi trigger, event ya infected file admin ko delete ke baad phir bana deti hai

causes.title_en: Anyone can register, and new users get the administrator role
causes.title_hi: Koi bhi register kar sakta hai, aur naye user ko administrator role milta hai

fixes.steps_en: After the evidence copy: in Users, delete the unknown admin and give its content to a real user (or delete its wp_users row and its wp_usermeta rows). Reset every real admin's password.
fixes.steps_hi: Saboot wali copy ke baad: Users mein anjaan admin delete karo aur uska content asli user ko do (ya wp_users ki row aur uski wp_usermeta rows hatao). Har asli admin ka password reset karo.

fixes.steps_en: Delete the wp_usermeta capability/user_level rows that give admin to unknown or missing user ids.
fixes.steps_hi: wp_usermeta ki woh capability/user_level rows hatao jo anjaan ya gayab user id ko admin banati hain.

fixes.steps_en: Remove the trigger/event first (see the triggers and events playbooks), replace WordPress core files with a fresh copy and scan themes/plugins; then delete the admin again.
fixes.steps_hi: Pehle trigger/event hatao (triggers aur events playbook dekho), WordPress core files fresh copy se badlo aur themes/plugins scan karo; phir admin dobara delete karo.

fixes.steps_en: Set users_can_register to 0 (or default_role back to subscriber) in Settings > General.
fixes.steps_hi: Settings > General mein users_can_register 0 karo (ya default_role wapas subscriber).

verify.en: The admin list holds only people you know, and stays that way after a day (nothing re-creates it).
verify.hi: Admin list mein sirf jaane-pehchane log hain, aur ek din baad bhi waisa hi hai (koi dobara nahi banata).

fixes.steps_en: After the evidence copy: lock it first (ALTER USER ... ACCOUNT LOCK / ALTER ROLE ... NOLOGIN), end its sessions, then DROP USER / DROP ROLE (reassign or drop what it owns first in PostgreSQL).
fixes.steps_hi: Saboot wali copy ke baad: pehle lock karo (ALTER USER ... ACCOUNT LOCK / ALTER ROLE ... NOLOGIN), uske sessions band karo, phir DROP USER / DROP ROLE (PostgreSQL mein pehle uski cheezein reassign/drop karo).

fixes.steps_en: REVOKE the extra rights so the app user has only SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on its own database (ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER; REVOKE pg_execute_server_program ...), then change its password.
fixes.steps_hi: Extra rights REVOKE karo taaki app user ke paas sirf apne database pe SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ho (ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER; REVOKE pg_execute_server_program ...), phir password badlo.

fixes.steps_en: Confirm with the team, then lock or drop it; keep one named account per person or app.
fixes.steps_hi: Team se confirm karo, phir lock ya drop karo; har insaan ya app ka ek apna naam wala account rakho.

verify.en: Every account and grant in the list is known, app accounts have only data rights, and no account allows any host ('%') unless needed.
verify.hi: List ka har account aur grant jaana-pehchana hai, app accounts ke paas sirf data rights hain, aur koi account bina zaroorat kisi bhi host ('%') se nahi aata.

causes.title_en: A trigger fires on a normal action (new comment/order/user) and secretly adds an admin or changes data
causes.title_hi: Ek trigger normal kaam (naya comment/order/user) pe chalta hai aur chupke se admin banata ya data badalta hai

fixes.steps_en: Save its definition (SHOW CREATE TRIGGER / pg_get_triggerdef) as evidence, then DROP TRIGGER it; drop the function it called (PostgreSQL) and undo what it created (users, rows).
fixes.steps_hi: Uski definition (SHOW CREATE TRIGGER / pg_get_triggerdef) saboot ke liye save karo, phir DROP TRIGGER karo; jo function woh chalata tha use hatao (PostgreSQL) aur jo usne banaya (users, rows) use undo karo.

fixes.steps_en: Save it, then DROP EVENT TRIGGER (needs a superuser) and check who owns it: that role is likely compromised too.
fixes.steps_hi: Save karo, phir DROP EVENT TRIGGER (superuser chahiye) aur dekho owner kaun hai: woh role bhi shayad compromised hai.

fixes.steps_en: Keep it; write down which plugin/app owns it so the next check is quick.
fixes.steps_hi: Rehne do; likh lo kaunse plugin/app ka hai taaki agla check jaldi ho.

verify.en: The trigger list has only triggers you can name the owner of, and new comments/orders no longer create users or change data.

causes.title_en: A script/link was added to many existing posts at once
causes.title_hi: Bahut saare purane posts mein ek saath script/link jod diya gaya

causes.title_en: The attacker created many new spam pages/posts
causes.title_hi: Attacker ne bahut saare naye spam pages/posts bana diye

fixes.steps_en: Best: restore posts from a clean backup taken before the injection day. Otherwise remove the exact injected snippet from the affected rows after approval (we show every changed row; Undo keeps the old text). Don't run a blind search-replace on serialized data in wp_options/wp_postmeta: it breaks it.
fixes.steps_hi: Sabse accha: injection wale din se pehle ke saaf backup se posts restore karo. Warna approval ke baad affected rows se wahi daala gaya code hatao (har badli row dikhegi; Undo purana text rakhta hai). wp_options/wp_postmeta ke serialized data pe andha search-replace mat chalao: woh toot jata hai.

fixes.steps_en: Delete the spam posts by the date range/author they share (after reviewing the list), then ask Google to re-crawl and remove them from search.
fixes.steps_hi: List dekh ke, spam posts ko unki common date range/author se delete karo, phir Google se re-crawl karwao taaki search se hatein.

fixes.steps_en: Remove the source first: replace core files, scan themes/plugins, and check the triggers/events playbooks; otherwise the cleaning is undone.
fixes.steps_hi: Pehle jad hatao: core files badlo, themes/plugins scan karo, aur triggers/events playbook dekho; warna safai phir se bekaar ho jayegi.

verify.en: The check finds no injected script/link in posts, the spam page count is back to normal, and it stays clean for a few days.
verify.hi: Check ko posts mein koi daala hua script/link nahi milta, spam pages normal ho gaye, aur kuch din tak saaf rehta hai.

fixes.steps_en: Find the earliest sign (oldest unknown admin, first injected post, trigger CREATED time). Restore the backup from before that date into a NEW database first, run the hacked checks on it, then switch the app to it. With binlog/WAL you can replay up to just before the attack (point-in-time recovery). Orders/sign-ups made after the backup must be copied over by hand.
fixes.steps_hi: Sabse pehla nishaan dhoondo (sabse purana anjaan admin, pehla infected post, trigger ka CREATED time). Us date se pehle ka backup pehle ek NAYE database mein restore karo, us pe hacked checks chalao, phir app ko us pe shift karo. binlog/WAL ho to attack se theek pehle tak replay ho sakta hai (point-in-time recovery). Backup ke baad ke orders/sign-ups haath se copy karne honge.

fixes.steps_en: Pick an older backup, or clean the restored copy with the triggers/events/admin/spam playbooks before going live. And close the way in, or it will happen again.
fixes.steps_hi: Aur purana backup lo, ya live karne se pehle restored copy ko triggers/events/admin/spam playbooks se saaf karo. Aur andar aane ka raasta band karo, warna phir hoga.

fixes.steps_en: Ask your hosting provider for their snapshots; otherwise clean the current database in place with the playbooks. Then set up daily backups stored away from the server and test a restore.
fixes.steps_hi: Hosting provider se unke snapshots maango; warna playbooks se current database ko wahin saaf karo. Phir roz ka backup server se alag jagah rakho aur restore test karo.

verify.en: The restored database passes all the hacked checks (no unknown admins, triggers, events, spam) and the site works with today's real data copied in.
verify.hi: Restored database saare hacked checks pass karta hai (koi anjaan admin, trigger, event, spam nahi) aur aaj ka asli data copy karke site chal rahi hai.

diagnose.sql: SELECT ID, post_type, post_status, post_title, post_modified FROM wp_posts WHERE post_content LIKE '%<script%' OR post_content LIKE '%<iframe%' OR post_content LIKE '%display:none%' OR post_content LIKE '%eval(%' OR post_content LIKE '%fromCharCode%' ORDER BY post_modified DESC LIMIT 50
diagnose.look_for: posts/pages carrying hidden links or scripts; many posts changed at the same minute is a mass injection

diagnose.sql: SELECT TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_TIMING, CREATED, DEFINER, LEFT(ACTION_STATEMENT, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.TRIGGERS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: a trigger nobody on your team made, especially on comments/users/usermeta/posts/orders, or one that writes into a users table

diagnose.sql: SELECT EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME, DEFINER, STATUS, EVENT_TYPE, INTERVAL_VALUE, INTERVAL_FIELD, CREATED, LAST_EXECUTED, LEFT(EVENT_DEFINITION, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.EVENTS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: scheduled events you didn't create (they can re-add a user, re-insert spam or delete data every few minutes)

diagnose.sql: SELECT ROUTINE_SCHEMA, ROUTINE_NAME, ROUTINE_TYPE, DEFINER, SECURITY_TYPE, CREATED, LAST_ALTERED FROM information_schema.ROUTINES WHERE ROUTINE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('sys', 'mysql') ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: procedures/functions with names you don't recognise, recently created, or with an unknown DEFINER

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE, IS_GRANTABLE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: accounts you don't know, '%' hosts (any computer), and SUPER / FILE / GRANT OPTION / CREATE USER given to app users

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('bind_address', 'skip_networking', 'port', 'require_secure_transport', 'local_infile', 'secure_file_priv')
diagnose.look_for: bind_address 0.0.0.0 or * (open to every network), local_infile ON, secure_file_priv empty

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin, rolreplication, rolbypassrls, rolvaliduntil FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname NOT LIKE 'pg\_%' ORDER BY rolsuper DESC, rolname
diagnose.look_for: a login role you don't know, or extra roles with superuser / createrole / bypassrls

diagnose.sql: SELECT g.rolname AS powerful_role, r.rolname AS member FROM pg_auth_members m JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = m.member JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid WHERE g.rolname IN ('pg_execute_server_program', 'pg_read_server_files', 'pg_write_server_files', 'pg_signal_backend', 'pg_read_all_data', 'pg_write_all_data')
diagnose.look_for: an app or unknown role allowed to run server programs or read/write server files

diagnose.sql: SELECT t.tgrelid::regclass AS on_table, t.tgname, t.tgfoid::regproc AS runs_function, t.tgenabled FROM pg_trigger t WHERE NOT t.tgisinternal ORDER BY 1
diagnose.look_for: a trigger you don't know, especially one running a function you didn't write

diagnose.sql: SELECT evtname, evtevent, evtowner::regrole AS owner, evtfoid::regproc AS runs_function, evtenabled FROM pg_event_trigger
diagnose.look_for: any event trigger you didn't create (they fire on CREATE/DROP/ALTER in the whole database)

diagnose.sql: SELECT n.nspname AS schema, p.proname AS function, r.rolname AS owner, l.lanname AS language, p.prosecdef AS security_definer FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = p.proowner JOIN pg_language l ON l.oid = p.prolang WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema') ORDER BY n.nspname, p.proname
diagnose.look_for: functions with odd names, written in C or an untrusted language (plpython3u, plperlu), or SECURITY DEFINER owned by a superuser

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('listen_addresses', 'port', 'ssl', 'password_encryption', 'log_connections', 'log_statement')
diagnose.look_for: listen_addresses '*' (open to every network), md5 passwords, connection logging off

causes.title_en: Something the attacker left is still there (account, trigger, event, injected content)
causes.title_hi: Attacker ki chhodi koi cheez abhi bhi hai (account, trigger, event, daala hua content)

causes.title_en: The way in is still open (same passwords, open port, outdated plugin), so it comes back
causes.title_hi: Andar aane ka raasta abhi bhi khula hai (wahi password, khula port, purana plugin), isliye wapas aata hai

causes.title_en: All checks are clean
causes.title_hi: Saare checks saaf hain

fixes.steps_en: Open the matching playbook for each finding and remove it, then run these checks again.
fixes.steps_hi: Har finding ke liye uska playbook kholo aur hatao, phir yeh checks dobara chalao.

fixes.steps_en: Change passwords again AFTER cleaning, update WordPress/plugins/themes, remove unused plugins, close the database port, and give the app user only data rights.
fixes.steps_hi: Safai ke BAAD password phir se badlo, WordPress/plugins/themes update karo, bekaar plugins hatao, database port band karo, aur app user ko sirf data rights do.

fixes.steps_en: Save today's results as the 'known good' list and run the checks weekly; any new account/trigger/event is then easy to spot.
fixes.steps_hi: Aaj ke results 'known good' list ki tarah save karo aur har hafte checks chalao; koi naya account/trigger/event turant dikh jayega.

verify.en: Two runs a few days apart show the same known accounts, triggers, events and settings, and no injected content.
verify.hi: Kuch din ke gap pe do baar check chalane pe wahi jaane-pehchane accounts, triggers, events aur settings dikhte hain, aur koi daala hua content nahi.

causes.title_en: Encoded/obfuscated code or a script was saved in an option (widgets, theme options, header/footer code, a fake plugin option)
causes.title_hi: Encoded/chhupa code ya script kisi option mein save kiya gaya (widgets, theme options, header/footer code, nakli plugin option)

causes.title_en: It's your own tracking/analytics or ad code added on purpose
causes.title_hi: Yeh aapka apna tracking/analytics ya ad code hai jo jaan-boojh ke dala

fixes.steps_en: Save the option value as evidence, then remove the script through the WordPress screen that owns it (widget, theme options) or delete the fake option after approval (Undo kept). Don't text-replace serialized values. Then look for the file/plugin that wrote it.
fixes.steps_hi: Option ki value saboot ke liye save karo, phir jis WordPress screen ka woh option hai (widget, theme options) wahan se script hatao ya approval ke baad nakli option delete karo (Undo rehta hai). Serialized values pe text-replace mat karo. Phir woh file/plugin dhoondo jisne ise likha.

fixes.steps_en: Keep it and write down what it is.
fixes.steps_hi: Rehne do aur likh lo kya hai.

verify.en: The check finds no unknown script/encoded code in options, and the popups/redirects are gone in a private browser window.
verify.hi: Check ko options mein koi anjaan script/encoded code nahi milta, aur private browser window mein popups/redirect band hain.
